key_insight: RAPID turns a single human demonstration into a robot program by using an agentic code-generation loop that can automatically test, verify, and refine the program. This brings the productivity of coding agents to robot learning and control.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to reliably teach robots new tasks from only one visual demonstration, without requiring extensive manual programming, large datasets, or repeated human correction.
method: Start from a single visual demonstration and translate it into an initial robot program.
Use a testable task specification plus robot action primitives to automatically verify whether the program works.
Iteratively refine the code through an agentic loop until the generated robot behavior matches the demonstrated task.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, RAPID offers a practical path to faster robot skill acquisition with less manual engineering. It suggests that code-centric agent workflows can make robot programming more scalable, debuggable, and data-efficient.

paper_title: RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations
paper_authors: Yuyao Liu, Jiayuan Mao, David Hsu, Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Tomás Lozano-Pérez
